area_context: How much the household's survey area and the nearest areas raise or lower its risk, compared with an average area. The graph model learns this from households surveyed there.
w4_region: Region where the household lives (2018 regional boundaries; SNNP is shown as one region).
is_agricultural: Whether the household farms. The model is designed for farming households only.
n_holders: Number of household members who manage their own plots of land.
hh_size: Children + working-age members + elderly members. Calculated by the app.
n_children: Number of children (under 15) in the household.
n_elderly: Number of members aged 65 or older.
dependency_ratio: Calculated automatically from the number of children, elderly and working-age members: (children + elderly) divided by working-age members.
head_age: Age in years of the person who heads the household.
head_is_male: Yes if the household head is male, No if female.
share_female: Fraction of household members who are female (0 to 1). Example: 3 of 6 members = 0.5.
prior_fi_any: Calculated automatically from the three 2018 food questions. Shown only because the model uses it.
prior_fi_score: Calculated automatically: how many of the three 2018 food questions (worry about food, everyone eats the same food, food shortage in the past year) were answered Yes.
prior_fi_s8q01: Official question: "Did you worry that your household would not have enough food in the last 7 days?"
prior_fi_s8q04: Official question: "Do all household members eat roughly the same diet?" Yes means men, women and children eat the same kinds of food.
prior_fi_s8q06: Official question: "In the last 12 months, have you been faced with a situation when you didn't have enough food to feed the household?"
prior_fi_days: Same as the question about relying on less preferred or cheaper food in the past 7 days.
prior_fi_rcsi: Calculated automatically from the 7-day coping questions (cheaper food, borrowing, smaller portions, adults eating less, fewer meals), weighted by seriousness. 0 = never had to cut back; 56 = did all of these every day.
prior_fi_coping_days: Calculated automatically: total days across all eight coping questions in the past 7 days.
prior_fi_coping_breadth: Calculated automatically: how many of the eight coping behaviours were used at least once in the past 7 days.
prior_fi_coping_max: Calculated automatically: the most days any single coping behaviour was used in the past 7 days.
prior_fi_coping_severe_days: Calculated automatically: days with no food in the house plus days without eating all day, in the past 7 days.
prior_fi_coping_severe_any: Calculated automatically: Yes if the household had no food, or went a whole day without eating, on any of the past 7 days.
prior_fi_cope_less_preferred: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to rely on less preferred foods? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_limit_variety: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to limit the variety of foods eaten? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_limit_portion: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to limit portion size at meal-times? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_fewer_meals: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to reduce the number of meals eaten in a day? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_restrict_adult: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to restrict consumption by adults so children could eat? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_borrow_food: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to borrow food or rely on help from friends or relatives? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_no_food: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to have no food of any kind in the house? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_cope_whole_day: In the past 7 days, on how many days (0–7) did the household have to go a whole day and night without eating? From the 2018/19 food-security questions.
prior_fi_meals_adult: How many meals, including breakfast, members aged 5 and over usually ate per day.
prior_fi_meals_child: How many meals young children (6–59 months) usually ate per day. Leave Unknown if there are no young children.
prior_fi_has_child_meals: Calculated automatically from the children's meals question.
cons_total_annual: Total value of everything the household consumed in a year, food and non-food, including home-grown food, in Ethiopian birr.
cons_per_adult_eq: Yearly household consumption divided by adult equivalents, so households of different sizes can be compared. The main measure of how poor a household is.
cons_food_annual: Value of all food consumed in a year, bought or home-grown, in birr.
adult_equivalents: Household size where a child counts as part of an adult. Usually calculated by the survey team; leave Unknown if you do not have it.
cons_quintile: Where the household's spending per adult falls nationally: 1 = poorest 20%, 5 = richest 20%.
cons_food_share: Fraction of all consumption that is food. Poorer households usually spend a larger share on food. Example: 0.7 = 70%.
econ_any_assistance: Yes if the household received any aid, such as a safety-net programme, free food or cash support.
econ_psnp: Yes if the household takes part in Ethiopia's Productive Safety Net Programme.
econ_free_food: Yes if the household received free food distributions.
econ_n_asset_types: Count each type once: owning 2 beds and 1 radio = 2 types. Examples: radio, mobile phone, bed, table, sickle, plough, jerrycan.
econ_total_assets: Count every item: 2 beds + 1 radio = 3 items.
econ_borrowed: Yes if the household borrowed money or goods in the past 12 months.
econ_credit_refused: Yes if the household tried to borrow and was turned down.
econ_has_nonfarm_business: Yes if anyone in the household runs a business outside farming (trade, crafts, services).
econ_n_nonfarm_types: How many different non-farm businesses the household runs.
geo_dist_road: Kilometres from the household to the nearest main road. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_dist_market: Kilometres from the household to the nearest major market. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_dist_popcenter: Kilometres to the nearest town of 20,000 people or more. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_dist_admhq: Distance to the zone administrative centre, on the scale used by the survey's location data (0–0.6). Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_elevation: Height above sea level. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_slope_pct: Steepness of the terrain around the household. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_pop_density: People per square kilometre around the household. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_cropshare: Fraction of the surrounding land used for crops. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_rain_2018: Total rainfall in 2018 at the household's location. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_rain_2019: Total rainfall in 2019 at the household's location. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_rain_long_term_avg: Average yearly rainfall over many years at this location. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_ndvi_avg: Average vegetation greenness seen from satellites; higher = greener land. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_ndvi_max: Highest vegetation greenness in a typical year. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_ndvi_2018: Vegetation greenness in 2018. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_ndvi_2019: Vegetation greenness in 2019. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_wetness_index: How easily water collects on the land, from terrain shape. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_rain_anomaly_2018: 2018 rainfall divided by normal rainfall. 1 = normal, below 1 = drier than usual, above 1 = wetter. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_rain_anomaly_2019: 2019 rainfall divided by normal rainfall. 1 = normal, below 1 = drier than usual, above 1 = wetter. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
geo_ndvi_anomaly: Recent greenness divided by typical greenness. Below 1 = poorer vegetation than usual. Location data from maps and satellites (GIS). Leave Unknown if you do not have it.
diet_n_items_unknown: Number of foods eaten in the past 7 days whose source (bought, home-grown, gift) was not recorded.
diet_n_items: How many different food items the household ate in the past 7 days.
diet_cereals: Teff, maize, wheat, sorghum, barley or other grains, including injera and bread.
diet_pulses_nuts: Beans, lentils, chickpeas, peas, groundnuts and similar.
diet_seeds: Sesame, linseed, niger seed and similar.
diet_vegetables: Onion, kale, cabbage, tomato, peppers and other vegetables.
diet_fruit: Banana, mango, orange, avocado and other fruit.
diet_roots: Potato, sweet potato, enset/kocho, cassava and similar.
diet_eggs: Any eggs eaten by the household in the past 7 days.
diet_n_groups: How many of 9 food groups the household ate: cereals, pulses, oil seeds, vegetables, fruit, roots, meat/fish, dairy, eggs. A low number means a narrow diet.
diet_purchased_item_fraction: Fraction of the foods eaten in the past 7 days that were bought rather than home-grown or received.
diet_purchased_n_observed: Number of food items with a purchase recorded (used to judge how reliable the share above is).
diet_own_item_fraction: Fraction of the foods eaten in the past 7 days that came from the household's own farm.
diet_own_n_observed: Number of food items recorded as home-grown.
diet_gift_item_fraction: Fraction of the foods eaten in the past 7 days that were gifts or aid.
diet_gift_n_observed: Number of food items recorded as gifts.
diet_purchase_birr_7d: Money spent buying food in the past 7 days, in birr.
diet_spending_n_observed: Number of food items with a spending amount recorded.
land_total_area: Area of all fields the household farms, in square metres. 10,000 m² = 1 hectare; 1 timad is about 2,500 m².
livestock_tlu: Animals converted to one common unit (tropical livestock units). The app calculates it from the animal counts: cattle 0.6 on average, sheep or goat 0.1, chicken 0.01.
crop_diversity: How many different crops the household planted this season (for example teff, maize and beans = 3).
land_any_irrigated: Yes if at least one field the household farms is irrigated.
q_cattle_adult: How many adult cattle the household owns now: oxen, cows and bulls.
q_cattle_young: How many young cattle the household owns: heifers and young bulls, not yet adult.
q_calves: How many calves (young cattle under about one year) the household owns.
q_sheep_goats: How many sheep and goats together the household owns now.
q_camels: How many camels the household owns now. Enter 0 if none.
q_poultry: How many chickens and other poultry the household owns now.
q_horses: How many horses the household owns now. Enter 0 if none.
q_donkeys_mules: How many donkeys and mules together the household owns now.
q_bee_colonies: How many bee colonies (occupied beehives) the household keeps.
crop_any_damage: Yes if the crop on any field was damaged this season (drought, pests, flood, hail, disease, animals...).
harvest_any_shortfall: Yes if the harvest from any field was smaller than the family expected when they planted.
livestock_cattle: All cattle the household owned 12 months ago: bulls, oxen, cows, steers, heifers and calves together.
livestock_small_ruminants: Sheep and goats together that the household owned 12 months ago.
livestock_poultry: Chickens (cocks, hens and chicks) the household owned 12 months ago.
land_area_per_person: Total farmland divided by the number of people in the household. Calculated by the app.
livestock_tlu_per_person: Livestock units divided by household size. Calculated by the app from the animal counts.
